reason: The text portrays the Hebrews (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל/עִבְרִים) as enslaved in Egypt, dwelling in the land of Goshen within Egyptian territory. The narrative depicts them requesting temporary freedom to worship in the wilderness (בַּמִּדְבָּר), not possessing their own land. While Goshen is identified as a place where the Israelites dwell, this is presented as a location within Egypt where they are enslaved, not as territory belonging to them as a nation. The passage focuses on their deliverance from Egyptian bondage and freedom to worship, not on territorial possession or national land ownership.
